transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-07 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Devon (Redwood SE), Arjun (BrightHealth ML), Lena (BrightHealth DevOps), Samira (BrightHealth Security)

Summary (auto): quick onboarding status check, access verification for VPC and service accounts, plan for latency/cost benchmark, security questions about KMS and audit logs, agree next steps for runbook and benchmarks.

00:00:03 Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining on a wednesday, um quick agenda - 1) access and onboarding blockers, 2) results from the sample run we kicked off last week, 3) security follow-ups, 4) next steps.
00:00:18 Arjun: thanks, yep that works. we had a few folks on PTO so catching up.
00:00:25 Devon (SE): quick note - i validated the service account permission set on our end and pushed a small infra helper script, should make the VPC peering step smoother.
00:00:34 Lena: great, can you re-share that script? last time the script failed on our ci because of a missing route table perm.
00:00:42 Devon: yeah - i'll drop the link in the follow-up. it's the small terraform wrapper plus a helper that sets the iptable rules, i think the missing perm is the -- oh sorry, the ec2:CreateRoute permission.
00:00:58 Samira: before we get too far, security - we still need clarity on KMS key usage and audit log retention. production data needs to be encrypted with our key and we need at least 90 days of audit logs, preferably pushed to our splunk instance.
00:01:12 Maya: understood. on KMS we support customer-managed keys via integrations with your cloud KMS; i'll include the config snippet. audit logs - we have a log export that can forward to splunk or S3 with lifecycle; i'll put the retention recommendations in the pack.
00:01:27 Arjun: perfect. on the sample run, quick status: we sent ~10k tokens through the pipeline yesterday - latency was okay for dev but we really need p95 under 500ms for the UI use-case.
00:01:40 Devon: quick clarification - are you talking about single-turn chat generation with 1k context or multi-turn with kv cache?
00:01:46 Arjun: multi-turn, because users often have previous medical context, so the kv cache matters.
00:01:52 Devon: okay that matters for batching and caching settings - our default continuous batching will help throughput but can add a tail to p95. for p95 under 500ms we recommend pinning a smaller model variant or using dedicated capacity with a low-latency kernel set.
00:02:07 Arjun: right, cost vs latency tradeoff - we need to show mgmt the numbers. can you include cost per 1k tokens for both hosted and dedicated?
00:02:15 Maya: yes we'll include an estimated cost sheet. devon - can you run the sample with the dedicated-profile sim and the hosted-profile so we have side-by-side?
00:02:23 Devon: yup, i'll run both and include p50/p95/p99 plus token cost. i'll also test with and without kv cache enabled for the session caching behavior.
00:02:36 Lena: about network setup - our infra team needs the exact outbound ports and cidr ranges to open. we asked for the cidr list last week but haven't got the peering window scheduled.
00:02:47 Maya: apologies, i thought we had confirmation. i'll re-send the CIDR ranges right after this call. can we lock a peering window for monday morning (2026-10-12)?
00:02:57 Lena: monday morning works, please ensure it's before 10am our time.
00:03:04 Samira: and one more security thing - does Redwood support customer-managed HSM for key storage or only cloud KMS integrations?
00:03:11 Maya: currently we support cloud KMS integrations (GCP/AWS/Azure) and customer-managed keys there. HSM direct integration is available as part of the private deployment workstream but not on the hosted pilot. i'll flag that as a note.
00:03:26 Samira: okay that's fine for pilot but need to note for procurement.
00:03:30 Arjun: any surprises from your side, devon, from the logs of the sample run?
00:03:35 Devon: a couple of things - we saw occasional tokenization mismatches on a handful of medical abbreviations, the tokenizer fell back to subword splits which slightly increased token count. and there was one spike where batching delayed a request ~1.2s - looks like a batching window interaction with long-running requests.
00:03:55 Arjun: hmm tokenizer is important - can we pin the tokenizer options or force a specific tokenization to match the production preprocessor?
00:04:02 Devon: yes we can add a preprocessing step or use our tokenizer override config. that'll reduce token expansion. i'll include the override in the benchmark run.
00:04:10 Maya: also want to confirm retention and data flow - are you sending tokens back to us for eval? we only store minimal logs for debugging unless you opt in to longer retention.
00:04:19 Arjun: we won't opt in to retention beyond debug logs, but we will need reproducible traces for any regression investigations.
00:04:25 Devon: that's standard - we produce trace IDs and a minimal trace export you can ingest into your observability. we'll strip PII in debug exports by default.
00:04:35 Samira: please ensure PII redaction is documented; until we see the doc we'll treat that as an open item.
00:04:40 Maya: noted. i'll include the redaction behavior and sample privacy policy excerpt.
00:04:47 Arjun: timeline question - management wants a 4-week pilot with a go/no-go after week 4. is that still aligned?
00:04:55 Maya: yes, that's what we discussed. the pilot is 4 weeks from first production-like benchmark. we should aim to finish the infra peering and run the benchmarks by 2026-10-13 so you have two weeks of evaluation and buffer.
00:05:06 Lena: ok makes sense. one more infra detail - do we need NAT egress or direct peering? we prefer peering for lower jitter.
00:05:14 Devon: peering is supported and preferred for low latency; NAT egress works but will add variability. we'll provide the exact route table changes.
00:05:22 Samira: about compliance - do you have an audit log schema for requests (who, what, when)? our auditors will want that.
00:05:29 Maya: yes there's an audit schema; i'll attach it. it includes request id, tenant id, redwood route, timestamp, and outcome. we can map fields to your auditor spec if needed.
00:05:40 Arjun: CX question - for canary rollouts, is there an automatic fallback if the new model exceeds latency thresholds?
00:05:46 Devon: yes - our rollout policies support automatic fallback to a previous model variant or to a cheaper fallback model and can be configured to trigger on p95 or error rate. we'll share the rollout snippet.
00:05:58 Maya: i want to call out one small risk - because you're testing multi-turn chat, the KV cache size will affect memory on dedicated pools; we might need to recommend a quantization profile to reduce footprint if you go to smaller GPUs.
00:06:12 Arjun: noted - can you recommend quantization and a few model variants that balance p95 < 500ms and cost?
00:06:18 Devon: yes, i'll include a recommendation table in the benchmark output: 8-bit quantized variant + dedicated small pool vs 4-bit for higher throughput, with expected token cost numbers.
00:06:29 Lena: are there any limits to request size for the hosted pilot? we saw some 6k token requests in the logs.
00:06:36 Maya: hosted defaults to 8k context for the pilot but we can patch-in larger contexts with notice; dedicated has configurable context size.
00:06:45 Samira: endpoint authentication - we prefer SAML-based service account federation to avoid key leakage. supported?
00:06:51 Maya: we support SSO for user access (SAML/Okta) and short-lived service tokens via STS for service accounts; i'll include the STS flow doc.
00:06:59 Arjun: great.
00:07:02 Devon: quick check - for the benchmark I'll run three scenarios: hosted default, hosted with kv disabled, dedicated with low-latency kernel. will produce p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, and token cost.
00:07:14 Arjun: perfect. if you can also include a run with our anonymization preprocessor that will help.
00:07:20 Devon: yep will plug that in.
00:07:24 Lena: timeline recap? peering done by 2026-10-12, bench results by 2026-10-13, security pack by 2026-10-09.
00:07:33 Maya: yes - i'll send the CIDR + peering times and the security pack right after this call.
00:07:40 Samira: two quick questions from me before we close - 1) retention of debug snapshots, 2) who owns incident response if pilot hits production - do we ship logs to you or to our SRE?
00:07:50 Maya: debug snapshots retained for up to 30 days by default, can be shortened. incident response - primary is your SRE, but we provide on-call SE support for the pilot and can have escalation to Redwood infra if it's platform-level. we'll include an ops runbook template.
00:08:05 Samira: thanks.
00:08:09 Maya: any other blockers?
00:08:12 Arjun: none from me.
00:08:14 Lena: none.
00:08:16 Maya: okay quick recap of next steps then - 1) Maya to send security pack + CIDR + audit schema by 2026-10-09, 2) Devon to run benchmark and share results by 2026-10-13, 3) Lena to confirm peering window and provide CIDRs by 2026-10-12, 4) Samira to send partial compliance questionnaire answers by 2026-10-12, 5) schedule runbook review for week of 2026-10-19.
00:08:40 Arjun: solid. thanks everyone.
00:08:42 Maya: thanks, we'll follow up in email.
00:08:46 Devon: i'll upload the benchmark artifacts to the shared drive and link in the follow-up.
00:08:50 Samira: bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., 'iptable' transcribed as 'ip table', 'kv cache' sometimes 'k v cache'), some overlaps. Links referenced: infra helper script (link shared in follow-up), security pack (to be shared), benchmark artifacts (to be uploaded).

End of transcript.
